subtitle: Five crowns, one battleground of memory: Pallava and Chalukya glory across a hundred years

panels.shot: epic wide-angle over the Deccan plateau at sunset
panels.action: Narasimhavarman I Mamalla stands in royal armor on a rocky height, Deccan plains stretching behind him toward Kanchipuram and Vatapi, sky burning gold as if holding many wars and dynasties in its light.

dialogue.text: In the age of Pallavas and Chalukyas, between Kanchipuram and Vatapi, war and poetry wrestled for a century over the right to remember India’s Deccan.

i18n.hi: पल्लवों–चालुक्यों के दौर में, कांचीपुरम से वातापी के बीच, सौ साल तक दख़न की यादों पर जंग और कविता कुश्ती करती रहीं।

panels.shot: slow aerial drift over a map-like vision of peninsular India
panels.action: The land between the Krishna and the Kaveri appears like painted parchment: rivers glinting, trade routes traced like faint lines, hill-forts marked as dark knots in a web of power across the sixth–seventh centuries.

dialogue.text: By the early seventh century, the Deccan was a crossroads of salt and horses, temples and tax, where Pallava Kanchipuram and Chalukya Vatapi strained against each other over passes, ports and tribute.

i18n.hi: सातवीं सदी की शुरुआत में दख़न नमक–घोड़ों, मंदिर–कर का चौराहा था, जहाँ पल्लव कांचीपुरम और चालुक्य वातापी दर्रों, बंदरगाहों और नज़राने पर भिड़े थे।

panels.shot: low-angle interior of a temple-hall with sculpted pillars
panels.action: A stone-pillared hall glows with lamplight; Brahmins and poets sit on mats, palm-leaf manuscripts spread before them, while outside faint silhouettes of spearmen move past, hinting at the court’s double world.

dialogue.text: Kings fought with elephants and iron, but they ruled with words. Inscriptions, copper plates and carved praises turned battles into stories, and stories into rights over land and men.

i18n.hi: राजा लोहे और हाथियों से लड़ते थे, पर राज शब्दों से करते थे। शिलालेख, ताम्रपत्र और तराशी हुई स्तुति लड़ाइयों को कहानियों में और कहानियों को ज़मीनी हक़ में बदल देते थे।

panels.shot: majestic interior wide of Aihole temple complex courtyard
panels.action: The Aihole temple complex stands under a clear sky; a learned poet, stylized as Ravikirti, sits by a carved slab, stylus poised, as attendants hold fresh stone ready for royal inscription.

dialogue.text: At Aihole, Pulakeshin II’s poet Ravikirti shaped a long stone poem. The prashasti sang of Chalukya victories, including a proud account of a campaign against Pallava Mahendravarman near Pullalur.

i18n.hi: ऐहोल में पुलकेशिन द्वितीय के कवि रविकीर्ति ने पत्थर पर लंबी कविता गढ़ी। यह प्रशस्ति चालुक्य विजय गाती है, जिसमें पुल्ललूर के पास पल्लव महेन्द्रवर्मन पर चढ़ाई का गर्व भी है।

panels.shot: dynamic battlefield wide near a tank and village mounds
panels.action: Armored lines of Chalukya cavalry and elephant corps press forward across dusty ground near a water-tank and low village mounds, while a more slender Pallava host holds a ridge under a hazy southern sky.

dialogue.text: Around 618–619 CE, Chalukya forces pushed deep into Pallava country, meeting Mahendravarman near Pullalur. Ravikirti’s verse made that clash a turning point, praising his lord as the breaker of Pallava pride.

i18n.hi: लगभग 618–619 ईस्वी में चालुक्य सेना पल्लव प्रदेश में गहराई तक धँसी, पुल्ललूर के पास महेन्द्रवर्मन से टकराई। रविकीर्ति के श्लोकों ने उस भिड़ंत को मोड़ बना दिया, अपने नरेश को पल्लव अभिमान तोड़ने वाला बताया।

panels.shot: close-up on carved Aihole inscription surface
panels.action: The camera lingers on chiseled Nagari characters on weathered stone, lit sharply from the side so each groove stands out, the text flowing like a river of boasting metaphors and cosmic comparisons.

dialogue.text: In Aihole’s lines, Pulakeshin is the ocean overwhelming a Pallava river, the lion before frightened elephants. Yet scholars today see such images as courtly performance, not neutral reports from the field.

i18n.hi: ऐहोल की पंक्तियों में पुलकेशिन पल्लव नदी को डुबोता सागर है, सहमे हाथियों के सामने सिंह। आज विद्वान इन छवियों को दरबारी नाटक मानते हैं, मैदान का सीधा वृत्तांत नहीं।

panels.shot: somber medium shot of Narasimhavarman in a palace corridor
panels.action: Narasimhavarman I Mamalla, younger and bareheaded, stands in a shaded corridor of Kanchipuram’s palace, listening to messengers while temple spires rise beyond; his face is calm but his jaw tightens with resolve.

dialogue.text: When Mahendravarman’s fortunes faltered, his son Narasimhavarman inherited more than a throne. He took on a wound to family honor and a Chalukya rival whose stone claimed glory over Pallava defeat.

i18n.hi: जब महेन्द्रवर्मन की किस्मत डगमगाई, उसका पुत्र नरसिंहवर्मन ने सिर्फ़ सिंहासन नहीं, घराने की चोट भी विरासत में ली—एक चालुक्य शत्रु, जिसके पत्थर पर पल्लव हार की शान खुदी थी।

panels.shot: heroic low-angle wide at Mamallapuram shore
panels.action: Narasimhavarman stands on the rocky shore at Mamallapuram as waves crash; behind him, unfinished monolithic rathas rise from stone, artisans at work, fusing royal patronage of art with the energy of preparation for war.

dialogue.text: Under Narasimhavarman, Pallava power hardened. Kanchipuram’s temples grew, Mamallapuram’s rocks became shrines, and the king trained for campaigns that would carry Pallava standards north, towards Vatapi itself.

i18n.hi: नरसिंहवर्मन के हाथों पल्लव शक्ति सख़्त हुई। कांचीपुरम के मंदिर उठे, ममल्लपुरम की चट्टानें तीर्थ बनीं, और राजा ने ऐसी मुहिम की तैयारी की जो पल्लव ध्वजों को उत्तर, सीधे वातापी की ओर ले जाएगी।

panels.action: Within a carved-pillared council hall, Narasimhavarman sits alert on a low throne, circling advisers and generals around him; a scroll-map of routes to Vatapi lies open, weighed down by a dagger.

dialogue.speaker: pallavas_and_chalukyas
dialogue.text: We do not chase words in stone. We secure these roads and fields.

i18n.hi: हम पत्थरों की बात नहीं दौड़ते। हम इन राहों और खेतों को सुरक्षित करते हैं।

panels.shot: epic marching-army wide over Deccan uplands
panels.action: A vast Pallava host moves across upland scrub and rocky outcrops, banners snapping, Narasimhavarman riding at the center; in the far haze, the dark ridge-lines hint at the direction of Vatapi.

dialogue.text: By the early 640s, Narasimhavarman’s counter-offensives pressed north. Chronicles and copper plates remember a climactic turn: Pallava forces reaching Vatapi, the Chalukya capital itself, around 642 CE.

i18n.hi: 640 के शुरुआती सालों में नरसिंहवर्मन की पलटवार मुहिमें उत्तर की ओर धँस गईं। लेख और ताम्रपत्र एक चरम मोड़ याद रखते हैं: लगभग 642 ईस्वी में पल्लव सेना का खुद चालुक्य राजधानी वातापी तक पहुँचना।

panels.action: Seen from a high vantage, Vatapi’s hill-ringed city stands under stormy clouds; distant silhouettes of siege engines and ranks of soldiers approach the walls, with Narasimhavarman’s standard visible among them.

dialogue.text: Later Pallava records echo with pride that Vatapi was captured and Pulakeshin II defeated. The exact moves are lost to us, but the memory of Pallava endurance turning to triumph is clear.

i18n.hi: बाद के पल्लव लेख गर्व से दोहराते हैं कि वातापी जीता गया और पुलकेशिन द्वितीय हारा। चालें हमें नहीं मालूम, पर पल्लव धैर्य का विजय में बदलना साफ दिखता है।

panels.shot: interior throne-room shot at Vatapi with Narasimhavarman
panels.action: Narasimhavarman sits for a moment on a foreign throne in Vatapi’s audience hall, not gloating but thoughtful, as Chalukya regalia lie set aside and temple priests look on in uneasy respect.

dialogue.text: For Pallava poets, this was the answer to Aihole’s boasts: a southern king seated in the northern enemy’s court, the humiliation of Pullalur paid back, the balance of honor redrawn.

i18n.hi: पल्लव कवियों के लिए यह ऐहोल की शेख़ी का जवाब था: दक्षिण का राजा उत्तरी दुश्मन के दरबार में विराजमान, पुल्ललूर की बेइज़्ज़ती चुकाई हुई, सम्मान का तराज़ू फिर से खिंचा।

panels.shot: close-up of Narasimhavarman contemplating a copper plate grant
panels.action: In a quieter chamber, Narasimhavarman holds an engraved copper plate, its rings threaded together; a priest and scribe stand ready to record a temple grant, the battlefield victory translated into sacred patronage.

dialogue.text: Kuram copper plates and others praise Narasimhavarman as Vatapikonda, the conqueror of Vatapi, and tie his victories to land grants for temples. War flowed into worship and administration.

i18n.hi: कूरम के ताम्रपत्र और दूसरे लेख नरसिंहवर्मन को ‘वातापीकोंड’ यानी वातापी विजेता कहते हैं, और उसकी जीतों को मंदिरों को दी गई ज़मीन से जोड़ते हैं। जंग से पूजाअर्चना और राजकार चलने लगे।

panels.shot: serene temple interior medium shot in Kanchipuram
panels.action: Inside a Pallava-era temple at Kanchipuram, Narasimhavarman stands with folded hands before the deity, while sculpted walls show scenes of devotion; behind him, an inscription slab waits to receive text.

dialogue.text: In this age, Bhakti devotion deepened. Kings like Narasimhavarman placed their triumphs within the language of service to gods, presenting themselves as protectors of shrines and donors of sacred lands.

i18n.hi: इसी दौर में भक्ति और गहरी हुई। नरसिंहवर्मन जैसे राजा अपनी विजयों को देवसेवा की भाषा में रखकर खुद को तीर्थों के रक्षक और पवित्र भूदान के दाता दिखाने लगे।

panels.shot: time-lapse style wide of Deccan landscape shifting with new forts
panels.action: The same Deccan landscape is shown across different lights, as fortifications appear and fade, new banners rise, and roads spread outward, suggesting successive generations of Chalukya and Pallava rule reshaping space.

dialogue.text: Yet Vatapi’s loss did not end the story. Chalukya lines continued, Pallava power ebbed and rose, and the struggle over this corridor of hills and plains stretched into later decades and rulers.

i18n.hi: पर वातापी की हार पर कहानी ख़त्म नहीं हुई। चालुक्य वंश चलता रहा, पल्लव ताक़त उतर–चढ़ती रही, और पहाड़ियों–मैदानों की यह सँकरी पट्टी पर संघर्ष बाद के दशकों और नए राजाओं तक खिंचा।

panels.shot: dynamic battle-wide of later, smaller clash
panels.action: A later scene shows a more fragmented battlefield: different banners, leaner forces, and unfamiliar hill-forts, hinting at renewed contests as successors fight over the same passes that their grandfathers had bled for.

dialogue.text: Through the later seventh and into the eighth century, Chalukya pressure and occupation threats returned. Pallava kings faced raids and setbacks, their endurance tested anew beyond Narasimhavarman’s blazing moment.

i18n.hi: सातवीं सदी के उत्तरार्ध से आठवीं में कदम रखते हुए चालुक्य दबाव और क़ब्ज़े का ख़तरा फिर लौटा। पल्लव राजाओं पर नए हमले और मातें आईं, उनका धैर्य नरसिंहवर्मन के तेज़ दौर से आगे फिर आज़माया गया।

panels.shot: medium shot of a Rashtrakuta cavalry contingent riding
panels.action: A fresh northern cavalry contingent marked with Rashtrakuta emblems rides across the plateau, their arrival suggesting another power entering the field, altering the balance between older rivals.

dialogue.text: By the mid-eighth century, the Rashtrakutas emerged from the Deccan. Their rise helped Nandivarman II’s Pallavas recover ground against Chalukya claimants, adding a third voice to this long contest.

i18n.hi: आठवीं सदी के बीच तक राष्ट्रकूट दख़न से उभर आए। उनके उठने से नन्दिवर्मन द्वितीय के पल्लवों को चालुक्य दावेदारों के ख़िलाफ़ ज़मीन वापस लेने में मदद मिली—इस लंबी टक्कर में तीसरी आवाज़ जुड़ गई।

panels.shot: scholarly close-up of Velurpalaiyam copper plates being examined
panels.action: In a modern archive-like setting, gloved hands gently hold Velurpalaiyam copper plates; the engraved characters shine under soft light as notes and reference books lie open nearby.

dialogue.text: Velurpalaiyam and other Pallava plates speak of survival and recovery, just as Aihole’s prashasti sings of conquest. Today, historians read these not as simple reports, but as crafted performances of legitimacy.

i18n.hi: वेलुरपलायम और अन्य पल्लव ताम्रपत्र ऐहोल की प्रशस्ति की तरह विजय नहीं, बचाव और उबरने की कथा कहते हैं। आज इतिहासकार इन्हें सीधी ख़बर नहीं, बल्कि वैधता दिखाने का गढ़ा हुआ प्रदर्शन मानकर पढ़ते हैं।

panels.shot: wide shot juxtaposing Aihole stone and Pallava plates side by side
panels.action: A composition places the Aihole stone inscription and Pallava copper plates opposite each other on a table, like two voices in debate, with faint silhouettes of Kanchipuram and Vatapi visible behind them.

dialogue.text: Across five generations, Pallava and Chalukya courts turned the same roads and sieges into rival poems. When we listen to both, we glimpse a deeper history, where memory itself is a contested battlefield.

i18n.hi: पाँच पीढ़ियों तक पल्लव–चालुक्य दरबारों ने वही राहें और घेराबंदी को दुश्मन–दुश्मन कविताओं में बदला। दोनों को सुनें तो गहरी परत दिखती है, जहाँ याद ही एक और रणभूमि बन जाती है।

subtitle_i18n.en: Five crowns, one battleground of memory: Pallava and Chalukya glory across a hundred years
subtitle_i18n.hi: पाँच मुकुट, एक यादों का रणभूमि: सौ साल तक पल्लव–चालुक्य शान
